summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.1 -- RepositoryIdentity + DeploymentBinding First-Use Proposition Preparation Independent Verification. FINAL VERDICT: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- RI-D VALID. Independently reconstructed 149O.20L.7O's Transition-2 architecture and first-use proposition-preparation conclusions from primary source (repository_identity.py, hatp_bootstrap.py, hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py, hatp_class_b_conformance.py, hatp_mandatory_certification.py, HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md, HUMAN_APPROVAL_TRUSTED_PROVENANCE_CONTRACT.md) without treating 7O's report as an oracle. Reproduced uuid.uuid4()-only generation with no caller input/seed/persist-free mode; reproduced idempotency and fail-closed partial-write/malformed/symlink behavior via fresh disposable tempdir simulations. Built a full authority-conferral consumer inventory across every real importer of repository_identity (hatp_class_b_conformance, hatp_deployment_binding_admin, hatp_mandatory_certification, hatp_mandatory_cutover, hatp_signing_ceremony, hatp_ag_authority, hatp_rollback_consumption, human_approval_trusted_provenance, commands/init.py) and found no code path treats identity's mere existence as sufficient to grant authority. Located a stronger primary-source statement than 7O itself cited -- HBDC-REQ-068, which directly states repository-identity creation 'needs no approval' -- independently confirming Governance Classification A (non-authority descriptive/bootstrap state, no election required). Independently re-derived and selected model RI-D among RI-A/B/C/D on the same authority-precision/failure-isolation/auditability grounds 7O used, reaching the identical selection from a fresh comparison. Confirmed by disposable before/after execution that HBDC-REQ-042's failure reason changes from no_repository_identity_present to no_active_deployment_binding_matches_repository_and_root on identity creation alone, with satisfied remaining False in both cases (no compliance change from identity alone). Confirmed the HMIC implementation_scope_digest is provably unaffected by RepositoryIdentity creation via a disposable before/after digest computation, and that the resulting digest exactly matches the deployed value (65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8). Reproduced the audit-durability gap by actually executing the failure (monkeypatching append_provenance_event to raise) rather than reasoning about it from the docstring, and found a refinement not explicitly named by 7O: create_deployment_binding's idempotency comparison (_COMPARED_AUTHORITY_FIELDS) excludes election_reference, so a naive retry after an audit-emission failure can silently return ALREADY_SATISFIED without ever recovering the original creation's audit record or election linkage. Verdict remains NON-BLOCKING FOR FIRST USE, conditional on an explicit registry-read-back-and-reconcile procedure before any retry of a real create_deployment_binding call. Live read-only SSH to hac-dell (as codex, sudo -n only, no write verb) reconfirmed the entering baseline exactly unchanged (SHA b0840e96a7ffb12308e95828aa5927c3e7c770c0, RepositoryIdentity absent, DeploymentBinding absent, trust-store empty) and surfaced a concrete operational requirement not previously named this explicitly: codex (uid 1003) is not a member of group pcae and cannot access /opt/pcae/runtime/src at all without sudo; a future identity-creation step must execute as the pcae OS principal specifically (matching 7O's own diagnostic-invocation pattern), or the resulting 0600-mode file, created under root's identity via a naive sudo invocation, would be unreadable by the pcae principal that every downstream consumer runs as. Confirmed zero src/pcae/** drift between Mac HEAD and the deployed candidate SHA via git diff --stat (source remains current; no redeployment required). Independently re-read both existing CHGRs directly from their JSON records and confirmed neither authorizes RepositoryIdentity or DeploymentBinding creation; condition 7 of the current CHGR (chgr-71bd24f9d3d742d6baac772e480fc876) explicitly names RepositoryIdentity in its prohibition list, and condition 17 confirms first-use transition remains separately gated -- read as referring to the DeploymentBinding election specifically, not as itself requiring an identity-creation vote, since that would contradict HBDC-REQ-068's own controlling, more specific text. Confirmed via live Dell read that the production trust-store registry is completely empty (no principals, signers, authorities, or bindings enrolled at all) -- field-resolution verdict remains BINDING PROPOSITION STILL BLOCKED ON FIELD RESOLUTION for principal_id/signer_key_id/provider_profile/authority_scope, independent of and orthogonal to RI-D's validity, since no existing enrollment record exists anywhere to reference. No RepositoryIdentity, DeploymentBinding, election, CHGR, certification, Boundary C, Boundary A, HATP activation, or Dell mutation of any kind performed. Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7O.2 (RepositoryIdentity creation on Dell, unelected, pcae-principal-executed, + exact DeploymentBinding proposition drafting).
